MIT researchers figure out how to break Tor anonymity without cracking encryption | ExtremeTech

TLDR; Basically the technique is to set up a TOR entry node, count the packets coming in to determine what services a user is trying to reach using algorithms they developed. This would have to be on a lot of entry nodes to actually be very effective though.

"The attack targets the...entry nodes, as have several attacks in the past. Basically, the attacker sets up a computer on the Tor network as an entry node and waits for people to send requests through it. When a connection is established over Tor, a lot of data is sent back and forth. MIT researchers used machine learning algorithms to monitor that data and count the packets. Using only this metric, the system can determine with 99% accuracy what kind of resource the user is accessing (i.e. the open web, a hidden service, and so on)."
And the fix is equally simple: start sending dummy packets to confuse the algorithm.
That would add some overhead, and would probably waste the user's data usage (if they have a data cap). Cool idea though.

can determine with 99% accuracy

is one in one hundred reasonable doubt?

I'm pretty sure wikileaks revealed that the NSA was already using this method of detection. It was reported at least as early as last year and government agencies reportedly run many thousands of nodes. I'm surprised it took MIT this long to figure it out.

My bet is that MIT figured it out on contract for the Gvt - and they had to wait a set number of years before going public. Either that or they were allowed to go public because it's already being reported on.

The NSA's method was different and required a compromised entry AND exit node, thus only being useful for clearnet snooping. It also required access to the logs of the server being connected to. Basically it would use time to connect the Tor entry, Tor exit, and server connection events together to prove a specific IP is making the connection. That method, while more demanding, is possible because the delay is roughly the same until you change nodes. At least that's how I remember it when I read it, I'm no networking expert.

machine learning - is this a new buzzword? After reading the paper (btw here, please hide it more MIT) it looks more like a heuristic algorithm.

And the anonymity isn't actually broken (at least not fully), just because you know with a very high chance what the person is doing (browsing, watching videos, downloading) - because you still hide from the attacker if you a watching a completely fine cat video or an absolutely disturbing video of 90s Revival cover band.
